destination.name: Dharug National Park
destination.tagline: A Hawkesbury River park holding a convict-built road that is part of a World Heritage site.
destination.description: Dharug National Park covers 148.5 sq km on the Hawkesbury River and was established in 1967. It holds the Old Great North Road, built by up to 720 convicts between 1826 and 1836, and its Devine's Hill and Finch's Line sections were inscribed as part of the Australian Convict Sites World Heritage listing in 2010. Wisemans Ferry, where a free cable ferry has crossed the river since 1829, is the usual gateway. The park can be walked, cycled, paddled or camped.
whyVisit: Walk the convict-built Old Great North Road
Cross the Hawkesbury on the Wisemans Ferry

goodToKnow.title: No food in the park
goodToKnow.detail: There are no cafes or restaurants in the park, and the closest are in Spencer, so bring your own food.

goodToKnow.title: Ferry and car access
goodToKnow.detail: From anywhere but Wisemans Ferry the park is reached by car only, and the vehicle ferry across the Hawkesbury is free and takes about 3 to 5 minutes.

goodToKnow.title: Download the Convict Road app
goodToKnow.detail: NSW National Parks suggests downloading the Convict Road app before heading out on the Old Great North Road, where it acts as a guide along the walk.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, when milder weather suits walking or cycling the Old Great North Road and paddling the Hawkesbury.
